title: Acceptance check result block
description: The machine-readable definition of docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md §21 — what the acceptance session reports after it has looked at a finished plan's app (KIT-531, for the poller of KIT-324). The block is written by a model: it can name a problem, and it can never grant a pass, a budget or a merge.
$comment: DATA, NEVER AUTHORITY. The poller trusts the look tool's own record for what ran and what failed mechanically, and this block only for what the session judged on screen. `found-nothing` with a problem listed or a check that did not pass, `found-problems` with none, `could-not-check` with no reason, and a `reason` on any other outcome are all refused, so a result can never read as passed while it says otherwise.

schema.description: The marker. A reader that does not know it holds the plan and says could-not-check.

plan.description: The epic this result is about.

head.description: The pull-request head the session built, in full.

outcome.description: The session's own summary, held to `problems` and `reason` below.

ran.description: Each check, viewport and mode the session says it ran. The poller checks this against the look tool's record.

problems.description: Every problem it believes it saw. Empty only for `found-nothing` and `could-not-check`.

reason.description: Why it could not check. Required for `could-not-check`, and only then.

text.description: One line, at most 300 characters. The poller still neutralizes markers, fences and @-names before it embeds any of it.

result.description: As the look tool reported it. `could-not-run` is never a pass.

id.description: A short name for the problem. The poller refuses or merges a repeated one; this schema cannot check uniqueness.

screenshot.description: The name of the screenshot that shows it, as the check's `screenshot` step named it.

what.description: What is wrong, in one plain sentence.
